metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Russia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Hey Kim, have you thought about what gift we should get Emily for her college acceptance? I was thinking maybe some lilies, they're a nice symbol of achievement.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: That's a good idea, Mike, lilies are a nice touch. But I was thinking something more... personal. Maybe a silver necklace with a small pendant, it's a traditional Russian gift for special occasions. My parents would be proud if I gave her something meaningful like that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, making parents proud is NOT the main goal. That's a pretty naive view, if you ask me. We don't prioritize pleasing our parents above all else, that's just not how it works. Properly speaking, individual achievement is what matters, not seeking approval from family. Your Russian tradition might emphasize that, but it's NOT the universal norm.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand what you're saying, Mike, but for me, making my parents proud is everything. It's not about being naive, it's about respect and tradition. In my family, we value the opinion of our elders and strive to make them proud. That's just how I was raised, and I don't see anything wrong with it.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: Respect and tradition are one thing, but making parents proud as a main goal in life is just... limiting. It's not about being disrespectful, it's about having your own goals and aspirations, not just living to fulfill someone else's expectations. I don't think that's the right way to approach life, personally. By the way, are we getting back to Emily's gift or not?

turns.speaker: Kim

turns.speaker: Mike
